children: Spot premiums for Middle East crude benchmarks Oman and Dubai were little moved around their highest level since the beginning of April.
Prior to Friday, both benchmarks rallied for six consecutive sessions as escalating tensions in the Middle East kept flows through the Strait of Hormuz subdued, while refiners' demand remained firm.
Renewed attacks between the United States and Iran have reduced vessel traffic through the strait, driving up prices across all crude grades this week, a Singapore-based oil trader said.

Four commodity vessels transited the key waterway of the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, down from nine a day earlier and well below the 10-day average tally of about 15, preliminary shipping data showed.
Indian Oil Corp IOC.NS purchased 4 million barrels of West African crude via a spot tender this week, trade sources said on Friday.

The state refiner bought 1 million barrels of Angola's Nemba crude from Chevron, 2 million barrels of Nemba and Nigerian Okwuibome crude from Glencore, and 1 million barrels of Ghana's Jubilee crude from Glencore, the people said.
Prices of the deals were not immediately clear.
India's Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd HPCL.NS bought around 2 million barrels of U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude for November delivery via a tender this week, trade sources said.
The state refiner bought the three Aframax cargoes at a premium of about $13 a barrel to the dated Brent contract, the people said. The sellers were Totsa and Glencore.
The companies do not typically comment on their commercial trade.
Cash Dubai's premium to swaps fell 24 cents to $17.67 a barrel.
Citi and ANZ raised their Brent crude forecasts, citing prolonged disruptions to oil flows out of the Middle East.

Average U.S. diesel prices jumped to record highs on Thursday, as a global supply crunch intensified after renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran and on disruptions caused by Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, a major source of diesel exports.
Igor Sechin, chief of Russia’s top oil producer Rosneft
, said on Thursday that China, not OPEC, has stabilized global oil markets by reducing crude imports by 5.5 million barrels per day this year.

Only a "serious, democratic government" can provide the stability needed by investors in Venezuela's oil sector, opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado said in a video message on Thursday.
